name: When or if
subtitle: Use when for things that will surely happen or that happen every time. Use if for things that might happen, or might not: When I get home, I'll call you. If it rains, we'll stay in.
source: icanspeak Spanish original English text (grammar-b1 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: When I get home, I'll call you. — If it rains, we'll stay in.

qa.html: when: you are sure it will happen, or it happens every time. When the film ends, we'll go home. (It will end.) When it rains, the garden smells lovely. (Every time.) When I was ten, we moved to Cardiff. (One moment in the past.)
if: it might happen, or it might not. If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay in. (Maybe it will, maybe it won't.) If you see Zofia, tell her I called. You do not know yet.
After both words, use the present simple for the future, not will: When she arrives, we'll start. If he comes, I'll make tea. The will goes in the other part of the sentence.

Typical mistakes: ✗ If I get home, I'll call you. (you will surely get home) → ✓ When I get home, I'll call you. · ✗ When it rains tomorrow, we'll stay in. (maybe) → ✓ If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay in. · ✗ When I will get home, I'll call you. → ✓ When I get home, I'll call you.

concept.noteHtml: A test: will it surely happen? Then use when. Maybe, maybe not? Then use if. For a past event that really happened, you can only use when: When I was young, … For more about if sentences, see Conditionals. For other time words, see Time clauses. US: the same rules.

listen.text: When I get home, I'll call you.
listen.note: You will surely get home: when.

listen.text: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay in.
listen.note: Maybe it will rain, maybe not: if.

listen.text: When I was a child, we had a dog.
listen.note: A moment in the past: always when, never if.

hoeren.instruction: Listen and choose the word you heard.

If I have time, I'll call you.
I'll read a book while you cook.
When the film began, the lights went out.
If the weather gets better, we'll go out.

rounds.label: 1 · sure → when
rounds.instruction: You hear two sentences about something that will surely happen, or did happen. Join them with when.

example.prompt: The film ends. We go home.
example.answer: When the film ends, we go home.

items.prompt: I get home. I'll call you.
items.answer: When I get home, I'll call you.

items.prompt: The lesson ends. We'll have lunch.
items.answer: When the lesson ends, we'll have lunch.

items.prompt: I was ten. We moved to Cardiff.
items.answer: When I was ten, we moved to Cardiff.

items.prompt: The train arrives at six. I'll text you.
items.answer: When the train arrives, I'll text you.

items.prompt: She heard the news. She cried.
items.answer: When she heard the news, she cried.

items.prompt: We arrived. It was raining.
items.answer: When we arrived, it was raining.

rounds.label: 2 · maybe → if
rounds.instruction: Now it is only possible, not sure. You hear 'Maybe' and a sentence. Make an if sentence.

example.prompt: Maybe it rains. We'll stay in.
example.answer: If it rains, we'll stay in.

items.prompt: Maybe you see Tom. Say hello.
items.answer: If you see Tom, say hello.

items.prompt: Maybe we miss the bus. We'll take a taxi.
items.answer: If we miss the bus, we'll take a taxi.

items.prompt: Maybe it's sunny. We'll go to the beach.
items.answer: If it's sunny, we'll go to the beach.

items.prompt: Maybe you need help. Call me.
items.answer: If you need help, call me.

items.prompt: Maybe I'm late. Start without me.
items.answer: If I'm late, start without me.

items.prompt: Maybe she's tired. She'll go to bed early.
items.answer: If she's tired, she'll go to bed early.

exercises.title: when or if?
exercises.hint: Will it surely happen (or did it happen)? Then when. Maybe, maybe not? Then if.
exercises.hintHtml: whenIt will surely happen, it happens every time, or it happened once in the past.ifIt is possible, but you are not sure.

items.prompt: My train arrives at six. ___ I get to the station, I'll text you.
items.why: The train will arrive, so you will get there. Sure: when.

items.prompt: I'm not sure about Saturday. ___ it's sunny, we could go to the beach.
items.why: Maybe it will be sunny, maybe not. Not sure: if.

items.prompt: The film finishes at ten. ___ it finishes, we'll walk home.
items.why: The film will surely finish. Sure: when.

items.prompt: I don't know where Tom is. ___ you see him, tell him to call me.
items.why: Maybe you will see him, maybe not. Not sure: if.

items.prompt: Amira's wedding is next month. ___ the wedding is over, they'll go on holiday.
items.why: The wedding will happen. Sure: when.

items.prompt: We might have a test tomorrow. ___ we have one, I'll study tonight.
items.why: Maybe there will be a test, maybe not. Not sure: if.

items.prompt: ___ I was a child, we lived in Leeds.
items.why: A time in the past that really happened. Past moments always use when.

items.prompt: We may miss the last bus. ___ we miss it, we'll take a taxi.
items.why: 'May miss' means it is possible, not sure. Use if.

exercises.title: Match the beginning with the end.
exercises.hint: Click a clause on the left, then the part that fits on the right.

exercises.title: when or if? More mixed.
exercises.hint: Past moment, every time, sure or not sure? Two of the sentences ask about time or choice.

items.prompt: Yesterday I was so happy ___ I got your card.
items.why: It happened once, yesterday. A past moment: when.

items.prompt: Every winter, ___ it snows, the children go sledging.
items.why: It happens every time it snows. Regular: when.

items.prompt: Ask Mei ___ she wants tea or coffee.
items.why: This 'if' means 'whether': a choice between two things, not a time.

items.prompt: Can you tell me ___ the next bus leaves? I need the time.
items.why: You ask about the time: when.

items.prompt: Call me ___ you need any help. Maybe you will, maybe you won't.
items.why: Needing help is only possible. Not sure: if.

items.prompt: Every time ___ I visit my gran, she makes soup.
items.why: 'Every time' already points to something regular: when.

items.prompt: I'll call you ___ I land. My plane gets in at nine.
items.why: The plane will land. Sure: when.

sentences.hint: A moment in the past: when. Put the when part first.
Maybe you have time: if. Present simple after if.
A question: the when part comes at the end.
Maybe it rains: if. Then the main clause with will.
